indicator_definition: This indicator measures the standardised death rate from non-communicable chronic diseases, including cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes and chronic respiratory diseases. It is expressed as deaths per 100,000 persons, standardised to the European Standard Population (ESP 2013). Data are compiled by Eurostat from national causes of death statistics.
rationale: Non-communicable diseases are the leading cause of premature mortality in Europe. Reducing premature deaths from chronic diseases requires effective prevention, early detection and access to quality healthcare. Progress means a reduction in the standardised death rate from these diseases over time.
methodology_characteristics: Data are based on causes of death statistics from national death registries. The standardised death rate eliminates the effect of different age structures when comparing populations, using the European Standard Population (ESP 2013) as the reference. Data are reported annually to Eurostat.
indicator_name: Standardised death rate from chronic diseases
graph_title: Standardised death rate from chronic diseases
